purpose: Time-breakdown re-check after both crop-target bugfixes and the DRY refactor. Also uncovered that this script's PREVIOUS version had its own hand-duplicated, never-updated copy of the algorithm that still carried the original crop-target bug -- so it was rewritten to call the real, verified speculative_generate/speculative_generate_cached via monkey-patched timing wrappers instead of a second hand-written implementation.
interpretation: 3.594x is now consistent with p5_kv_cache_speedup.py's independently-measured 3.861x (seed 400) and 4.400x (seed 900) -- the previous profile run's 1.19x was an artifact of the stale duplicate implementation still carrying the original crop-target bug, not a real finding about caching overhead. Crop time is negligible (0.012s total across ~80 rounds for 400 tokens) -- it was never the bottleneck. Draft and target forward time both drop by roughly 3-5x under caching, which is where the real benefit comes from.
